citations.quote: For $a, b \in \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ the product $ab$ is defined by - $ab$ = the field product, when $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$; - $ab := +\infty$ when one of $a, b$ is $\pm\infty$, the other is $\ne 0$, and both are $> 0$ or both are $< 0$; - $ab := -\infty$ when one of $a, b$ is $\pm\infty$, the other is $\ne 0$, and one is $> 0$ and the other $< 0$; and **every product with one factor $0$ and the other $\pm\infty$ is left undefined**. The comparisons $> 0$ and $< 0$ here are taken in the order above, under which $+\infty > 0 > -\infty$.

derivations.claim: The empty domain has its unique empty output function. At each point of a nonempty domain, either a factor is zero, both are finite nonzero, or both are nonzero with at least one infinite; these disjoint cases each assign exactly one extended-real value.
The zero and finite clauses are invariant under swapping inputs, real multiplication is commutative, and agreement or disagreement of signs is symmetric; hence the function operation is symmetric.
On finite pairs the zero clause gives the real product when a factor is zero, and the finite-nonzero clause gives the real product otherwise.

For pairs with an infinite factor where scalar multiplication is defined, its sign rule is the same as the function rule. The four scalar-undefined zero-infinity pairs all receive zero under the function rule.

citations.quote: - If $a=0$ or $b=0$, set $(f\odot_X g)(x)=0$. - If $a,b$ are both finite and nonzero, set $(f\odot_X g)(x)=ab$, using the real field product. - Otherwise $a,b$ are nonzero and at least one is infinite. Set $(f\odot_X g)(x)=+\infty$ when $a,b$ have the same sign, and $(f\odot_X g)(x)=-\infty$ when their signs differ.
